A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SubZero research. All 24 pages of v2 and 27 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices 8.1–8.6, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning accuracies, convergence curves, resource measurements and ablations in Section 6 and Appendix 8.1.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds projection-source comparisons, gradient-spectrum analysis, scaling measurements and optimizer-integration experiments.

M1.justification: The main SubZero algorithms, low-rank perturbations, lazy updates and reshaping remain unchanged. Appendix 8.1 adds SubZO-AdaMU, maintaining low-dimensional momentum and transferring it between refreshed subspaces through a projection problem (Equations 17–19). v2 deferred evaluating this integration.

E1.justification: The classification, multiple-choice and question-answering datasets, non-differentiable objectives and appendix Winogrande tests are retained. New analyses reuse existing datasets and tasks; additional OPT sizes and model–dataset pairings change model configurations rather than data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 adds LOZO to the full-parameter OPT-13B comparison across eleven tasks previously reported in v2 Table 2. No LOZO LoRA row is added. Existing MeZO, ZO-AdaMU, S-MeZO, HiZOO, SGD and inference-based comparators remain.

E3.justification: Existing splits, prompts, search grids and training budgets are retained. Added experiments introduce projection-source controls, OPT-2.7B/6.7B resource measurements with stated FP32/BF16 settings, and shared learning-rate and perturbation-scale controls for SubZO-AdaMU. These extend the evaluation design without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands analysis of design choices and compatibility: random versus weight-, activation- and historical-gradient-derived projections (Table 1), gradient spectra across steps and layers (Figure 3), resource scaling (Table 11), and integration with ZO-AdaMU (Table 12/Figure 5). Existing orthogonality, rank/frequency, reshaping, batch-size, seed and Adam studies remain.

E5.justification: The same three seeds, 42, 0 and 1234, individual accuracies and averages appear in v2 Table 10 and v3 Table 13. No additional repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting practices are introduced. Figure 1's gradient-variance reporting is retained.

E6.justification: v3 adds LOZO scores, projection-source accuracies, gradient-spectrum and convergence curves, and scaling/integration results. The new WIC comparison reports SubZO-AdaMU at 61.1% accuracy and 27.07 GB versus ZO-AdaMU at 60.7% and 50.77 GB. In v2 Table 4 versus v3 Table 6, SubZero's cross-entropy RoBERTa scores change from 92.9 to 93.4 on SST-2 and 77.1 to 77.4 on MNLI. Most retained tables are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 3 replaces an assumed minimizer with an explicit lower bound, includes projection randomness in the expectation, and changes the iteration statement from Ω(d/ϵ) to O(d/ϵ). Its explicit step-size condition is omitted in v3 although still used in the proof. Appendix 8.6 also adjusts final summation indices; Theorems 1–2 and most derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: memory-efficient low-rank ZO fine-tuning, reduced gradient-estimation variance, convergence guarantees, compatibility with four fine-tuning schemes and advantages over MeZO. Added experiments and the optimizer extension do not redefine the stated main contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for activation-derived projections' poor performance and the hybrid optimizer's memory savings, and interprets scaling measurements as evidence of asymptotically negligible QR overhead. It removes v2's attribution of S-MeZO's inconsistent performance to threshold-based masking. Existing quantization and reshaping-theory limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents projection-source construction using activation statistics, damping and historical gradients, alongside experiment-specific ranks, update intervals and resource-test precision. Hardware, software, existing search grids, prompts and code access are retained. New details contain ambiguities: Table 1 assigns OPT-13B to RTE while Appendix 8.4 says SST-2, and Table 11's precision ranges overlap at 6.7B.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to LOZO, MLAE, Yong et al.'s preconditioned-gradient/AdaBK work and Yue et al.'s weak-dimension-dependency analysis. LOZO becomes an evaluated competitor, while the central positioning against MeZO and existing random-subspace approaches remains. Publication updates for S-RGF, AdaZeta and HiZOO concern already cited works.

P1.justification: The section hierarchy and most methodological prose remain stable. v3 makes localized introduction and results-discussion edits, condenses the S-MeZO discussion, adds appendix subheadings, revises the author/affiliation block and adds acknowledgments. The revision does not extensively rewrite the existing narrative.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation is substantially expanded and rearranged through new convergence panels, gradient-spectrum plots, a hybrid-optimizer curve and projection/scaling/integration tables. v2's memory/timing Table 5 moves to Appendix 8.1 as Table 10, and retained main tables are resized and repositioned. Original Figures 1 and 2 remain as Figures 1 and 4.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support for projection design and optimizer compatibility through direct alternative-projection tests and the SubZO-AdaMU study, and adds the relevant LOZO comparison. These improve the evidence behind the method while established benchmark conclusions remain stable. Benefits are limited by conflicting new setup descriptions in Table 1/Appendix 8.4 and Table 11, and by Theorem 3's omitted step-size condition despite its continued use in the proof.
